column3: Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew repeats “the wilderness of Ziph” as the search location; BSB replaces the second occurrence with “there.”
The Hebrew repeats Saul and the wilderness in describing his pursuit; BSB uses pronouns and “there.”
The Hebrew says David sent spies and then knew Saul had certainly come. BSB makes the verification the stated purpose of sending the spies.
The Hebrew repeats David as the one seeing the place; BSB uses “He.”
Abishai explicitly says he will go “down” with David; BSB leaves the downward direction implicit in his reply.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says he will not repeat the blow; BSB adds the explicit idea of necessity in “will not need to strike him twice.”

The Hebrew says the space between them was great; BSB specifies a “wide gulf.”
The Hebrew asks “Who are you who called to the king?”; BSB shortens this to “Who calls to the king?”
The Hebrew repeats “the king, your lord” as the threatened person; BSB uses “him.”
The Hebrew calls them “sons of death”; BSB renders the image as “deserve to die.”

The Hebrew wishes that the LORD may “smell an offering,” rendered “accept an offering” in BSB. The human instigators are called “sons of man,” rendered “men.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says Saul’s soul was precious “in your eyes”; BSB uses “you considered my life precious.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew’s first reference to delivery says simply “into a hand”; BSB supplies “my hand.”
The Hebrew says his soul was great “in my eyes” and wishes his own soul to be great “in the eyes of the LORD.” BSB renders both as valuing a life.
The Hebrew emphatically repeats both the doing and prevailing roots; BSB adds “great things” for the first and “surely” for the second. Saul returns “to his place,” rendered “home” in BSB.
